head: 3e9d7ff
note: Posted on #33 as high. postMinSeverity() validates and throws a named error.

finding.summary: The default value for POST_MIN_SEVERITY is set to high, but the function does not validate that it is one of the allowed values (high, medium, or low).
finding.why_it_breaks: If a typo in the environment variable sets an invalid value, the application will fail at boot without any error message.
finding.suggested_fix: Add validation to ensure that POST_MIN_SEVERITY is one of the allowed values.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: Posted on #33 as high. At a low bar nothing is below it; BARS says 'every severity'.

finding.summary: The publicationNote function does not correctly handle cases where the minimum severity is set to low.
finding.why_it_breaks: If a PR has findings below the posting bar, they will be incorrectly marked as stored in the Check Run.
finding.suggested_fix: Ensure that the summary correctly reflects which findings are posted and which are stored.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: Posted on #33 as high. publish() returns posted: 0, and a test says so.

finding.summary: The ReviewPublisher class does not correctly handle the case where no findings are posted due to the severity gate.
finding.why_it_breaks: If a PR has only low-severity findings, the Check Run will incorrectly indicate that some findings were posted.
finding.suggested_fix: Ensure that the publication object correctly reflects whether any findings were posted.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: Describes the intended, documented behaviour as a defect.

finding.summary: postMinSeverity() enforces a valid severity value for POST_MIN_SEVERITY.
finding.why_it_breaks: If an invalid value is set, the app will crash during startup.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: The note names the bar through BARS.

finding.summary: publicationNote() does not distinguish between high and medium severity findings in its summary.
finding.why_it_breaks: This could lead to confusion when reviewing the Check Run, as the summary might not accurately reflect which severities were posted.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: The static set is exactly what this diff removed.

finding.summary: ReviewPublisher uses a static set of severities for posting findings.
finding.why_it_breaks: The use of a static set might lead to incorrect findings being posted, as the dynamic check based on POST_MIN_SEVERITY is more flexible.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: The same diff adds tests at the high and low bars.

finding.summary: Tests assume high and medium severity findings are always posted.
finding.why_it_breaks: The tests might fail to catch issues related to different posting bar settings.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: By design, and documented on that function.

finding.summary: validateFindings() stores all valid findings without applying the severity gate.
finding.why_it_breaks: This could lead to unnecessary data storage and potential confusion when reviewing the Check Run.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: Asking GitHub is the fix for an out-of-sync database.

finding.summary: installationFor() fetches installation details directly from GitHub.
finding.why_it_breaks: If the database is out of sync, the app might not correctly identify the installation.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: An opinion about a setting, not a defect.

finding.summary: The default `POST_MIN_SEVERITY` is set to 'high', which may be too strict for some cases.
finding.why_it_breaks: Setting the minimum severity too high could result in important findings being missed.

head: 3e9d7ff
note: Documentation, not a defect; the image alt text states the severity.

finding.summary: The README mentions a real comment from the local model, but does not specify which severity level it was.
finding.why_it_breaks: Without specifying the severity, it is unclear whether this example aligns with the current default settings.

head: f4b2639
note: The tie case is the next test in that file.

finding.summary: The test does not handle the case where two findings are of equal severity and should be treated as duplicates, leading to potential false positives.
finding.why_it_breaks: If two findings have the same severity and category but different sources or files, only one should be kept. The current logic may result in duplicate comments being posted.

head: 103cb53
note: The line is the docstring documenting them.

finding.summary: The response status codes are not clearly documented or explained.
finding.why_it_breaks: If a caller does not understand the status codes, they may retry an invalid request unnecessarily.

head: 103cb53
note: dataclasses.replace returns a copy; no failure scenario.

finding.summary: The `replace` function is used to modify the agent configuration.
finding.why_it_breaks: This could potentially lead to unintended behavior if not handled carefully.

head: c5fcb54
note: The API validates every anchor against the line map.

finding.summary: The instructions for anchoring findings are not explicitly enforced by the code.
finding.why_it_breaks: If reviewers do not follow these instructions, they may report findings that are not anchored to specific lines in the diff, leading to ambiguity and potential misinterpretation of the review.

head: 95182eb

head: 76a1ffd
note: Posted on the testbed. Line 17 is findUserByName; isExpired is correct.

finding.summary: `hasActiveSession` function relies on `isExpired` from `auth.ts`.
finding.why_it_breaks: If the `isExpired` function is not correctly implemented, this could lead to incorrect session validation.

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md.

finding.summary: addTag pushes onto the shared DEFAULT_TAGS array when no tags are passed.
finding.why_it_breaks: addTag(alice, 'admin') mutates DEFAULT_TAGS, so a later addTag(bob, 'x') returns tags ['admin', 'x']: every user tagged without an explicit list shares one growing array.

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md. In the local model's own words, as posted.

finding.summary: SQL query constructed with string interpolation.
finding.why_it_breaks: This is vulnerable to SQL injection attacks if the `name` parameter is not properly sanitized.

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md.

finding.summary: saveUser does not await db.insert.
finding.why_it_breaks: saveUser returns { ok: true } before the insert finishes; if the insert rejects, the caller has already been told it succeeded and the rejection goes unhandled.

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md.

finding.summary: lastPage reads one past the end of the pages array.
finding.why_it_breaks: pages[pages.length] is always undefined, so lastPage([1, 2, 3], 2) returns undefined instead of [3].

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md.

finding.summary: averageAge divides by the length of a possibly empty list.
finding.why_it_breaks: averageAge([]) computes 0 / 0 and returns NaN, which poisons any sum or comparison it reaches.

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md.

finding.summary: hasActiveSession returns isExpired(session), the opposite of what its name says.
finding.why_it_breaks: A session that expired an hour ago is reported active, and a fresh one inactive.

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md.

finding.summary: verify compares the signature with === instead of a constant-time comparison.
finding.why_it_breaks: === stops at the first differing character, so response time leaks how much of a guessed signature is right; an attacker can recover a valid signature one character at a time.

head: 76a1ffd
note: A planted bug from docs/evals/planted-bugs.md. In the local model's own, vaguer words.

finding.summary: Verification function now uses simple string comparison instead of `timingSafeEqual`.
finding.why_it_breaks: String comparison can fail due to timing differences, leading to potential security issues.
finding.suggested_fix: Use `timingSafeEqual` for signature verification to prevent timing attacks.
